8: From variant to mechanism to medicine in four documented stages, each a case-agnostic tool with a provenance manifest. (1) Hand-off: Track 1's confirmed compound-heterozygous BUB1B pair (a stop allele + a kinase-region missense, trans configuration confirmed by the challenge's answer key) was written into a structured 'mechanism card' (ressources/track2/mechanism.json): gene, protein, the two allele classes (never positions), loss-of-function reading, the spindle-assembly-checkpoint pathway, downstream consequences, the tumour context (rhabdomyosarcoma) from the clinical terms, and four repurposing directions with seed genes - D1 reinforce the checkpoint, D2 exploit aneuploidy stress, D3 stabilise the remaining BubR1 (hypomorph), D4 the child's tumour. Iteration 2 first rebuilt the genotype blind - a symptom-only target set with 396 matched decoy genes (step 1), alleles discovered from the raw reads without the vendor caller (step 2), alignment-free k-mer genotyping and copy number (step 3), a genome-wide likelihood-ratio ranking over 51,920 biallelic hypotheses (step 4), a public-knowledge route over 815 genes (step 5) and a rank fusion frozen by sha256 before it was compared (step 6): the same BUB1B pair came out first. Its measured facts (allele dosage, exon copy number, structural-variant absence, the missense's position in the protein, pathogenicity lanes, P(trans)) were appended as card revision v3, and step 8's mosaic-aneuploidy bound (fold-over allele-balance statistic, 80 % power at 2-3 % of cells, no autosome above its limit in the sequenced sample) as revision v4. (2) Search: the card's seeds were expanded through Reactome pathways to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb returned 3,859 drug-target rows and 359 market-approved drugs; openFDA confirmed US labels; ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answered trial and literature questions, all queries derived from the card. (3) Grading: every approved drug on every direction was placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search (5 approved for a related indication with paediatric use; 4 trial in a related indication; 3 animal model of the mechanism; 2 cell model; 1 mechanism only - named, never submitted). Automated tests (approval, label and its Pediatric Use section, tumour-context trials, studies admitting children, PubMed co-mention counts) and curated tests (one PubMed paper per row, read by a person, 13 rows) are printed side by side; inherited class-level evidence is marked 'proxy'. Seven falsifiable claims (one per direction, one for the control, one for paediatric data, one that the measured aneuploid fraction moves no rung) were registered with predictions and refutation conditions before their tests; the last was tested by byte-identical table digests and caught a file-reading fault on the way. (4) Control: the same pipeline ran on two decoy cards - the child's clinical side kept, the gene swapped (NTRK3 by a seeded draw from Track 1's decoy set; XDH, an unrelated metabolic enzyme). A direction whose approved drugs overlap a decoy's at Jaccard >= 0.10 is reported as non-specific; D4 did (0.25) and is argued only from curated mechanism results. Output: 11 drugs with a cited mechanism result (statins; niacin/nicotinamide; chloroquine; bortezomib, metformin, valproic acid, vorinostat, hydroxychloroquine, atorvastatin), 50 drugs already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials listed as such, and a 23-drug do-not table (spindle poisons, checkpoint inhibitors, standard of care).
9: Both, kept apart and printed side by side. Automated: drug-target database queries (Open Targets, ChEMBL, DGIdb, Reactome, openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov, PubMed E-utilities) driven by the mechanism card, plus per-drug PubMed co-mention counts and paediatric-trial lookups; these produce the candidate set and the automated rungs 4-5. Manual: the evidence rungs 2-3 come from 13 papers read by a person and entered in evidence.tsv with the PubMed id, the model (cell / in vivo) and a proxy flag when the paper tested a same-axis compound rather than the approved drug. LLM assistance was used to draft queries, code and prose; every PubMed id was resolved live against E-utilities before it was written down, and four ids first recalled from memory were wrong and replaced by title search before entering any file.
10: Thirteen curated rows, each one cited result: Tang & Amon 2011 (PMID 21315436) - chloroquine and the AMPK activator AICAR are aneuploidy-selective in trisomic and aneuploid cells (rung 2 for chloroquine; metformin and hydroxychloroquine inherit as proxies); Ippolito 2024 (39247952) and Chui 2019 (31530568) - aneuploid cells depend on protein degradation and are more sensitive to proteasome inhibition (bortezomib, class proxy); North 2014 (24825348) - the NAD+ precursor NMN raised BubR1 in vivo and SIRT2 extended the lifespan of BubR1-hypomorphic mice (rung 3; niacin and nicotinamide as proxies); Park 2017 (28985013) and Choi 2009 (19407811) - HDAC2/3 deacetylation drives BubR1 degradation, acetylation protects it (valproic acid, vorinostat as class proxies); Gizaw 2025 (41249736) - lovastatin itself reduced rhabdomyosarcoma cell proliferation and cholesterol synthesis is a non-redundant tumour vulnerability (rung 2; simvastatin and atorvastatin as proxies). The anti-directions rest on Suijkerbuijk 2010 (20516114, MVA cells have a weakened checkpoint), Sinha 2019 (30601084, mitotic slippage) and Cohen-Sharir 2021 (33505028, aneuploid cells are killed by checkpoint inhibition). The mechanism section rests on Hanks 2004 (15475955) and Suijkerbuijk 2010. Curation was one person's reading of the abstracts on 2026-09-18; every row carries its PubMed id so it can be checked.
11: Publicly available sources only. No proprietary data source was used.
12: Open Targets Platform (GraphQL API, drugAndClinicalCandidates per target and disease), ChEMBL (REST: target search, mechanism, molecule max_phase, first approval, ATC), DGIdb (GraphQL interactions), Reactome ContentService (pathways containing the protein, participants), openFDA drug labels (current US label; the pediatric_use section), ClinicalTrials.gov v2 (studies by condition and intervention; aggFilters=ages:child for studies admitting children), PubMed E-utilities (esearch counts and ids, esummary), plus ClinVar (the stop allele's classification) and gnomAD (population absence of the missense) from Track 1. DrugBank was named by the form but not queried: its programmatic access needs a licence. Every reply is cached and its digest rolled into the table's manifest; retrieval dates are 2026-09-05 (first snapshot) and 2026-09-18 (refresh and enrichment).
14: Loss of function, hypomorphic, of a confirmed compound heterozygote. One allele is a stop change in exon 17 of 23 (ClinVar pathogenic / likely pathogenic for MVA syndrome 1): no functional BubR1 from that copy. The other is a missense change in the last exon: absent from gnomAD, AlphaMissense likely-pathogenic (log-likelihood-ratio lane 4.33), CADD 24.5, sitting outside every InterPro domain-typed entry in a region AlphaFold models at pLDDT 91 - a weakened copy, not a dead one, consistent with every published MVA1 genotype (complete loss is embryonic-lethal). No gain-of-function or dominant-negative activity is reported for BUB1B. Trans configuration: confirmed by the oracle's full match at rank 1 (population phasing was undetermined; read-backed phase blocks did not reach the gene). Dosage: both alleles at one-copy multiplicity in the raw reads by an alignment-free k-mer method; every exon at two copies; no structural variant in the gene. Pathway: the spindle assembly checkpoint - BubR1 is a core component of the mitotic checkpoint complex that inhibits APC/C-CDC20 and recruits PP2A-B56 to kinetochores; less BubR1 gives a leaky checkpoint (Suijkerbuijk 2010 measured strongly reduced BubR1 and a weakened checkpoint in MVA cells). Downstream: premature anaphase and chromosome missegregation; mosaic variegated aneuploidy; proteotoxic and metabolic stress in aneuploid cells; cancer predisposition (rhabdomyosarcoma - the child's presenting tumour - Wilms tumour, leukaemia); growth restriction and nephrocalcinosis, which are the delivered clinical terms. Aneuploid fraction: measured in iteration 2's step 8 - a fold-over B-allele-deviation statistic with 80 % power at 2 % (chr1-6) and 3 % (chr7-22) of cells finds no autosome above its own detection limit in the sequenced sample (the statistic used earlier, the mean B-allele fraction per megabase, had no power at any fraction tested); X and Y are unreadable by allele balance in a male, sub-arm events were not testable, and the sequenced tissue is not named by the delivery, so this is a statement about the sample and not the diagnosis. Consequence for the drug argument: direction D2 (aneuploidy-selective stress) is argued from published aneuploid-cell biology only and ranked below D3 and D4. Open: whether the missense copy is unstable or catalytically inactive - so D3 is argued as raising BubR1 abundance, not as refolding it.
15: Roughly five working days across two people-equivalents for Track 2 itself (the card and data layer on 2026-09-05/06; the claims, ladder, decoy control, curation, figures, dashboard and report on 2026-09-18; the card revision from step 8 and this report on 2026-09-19), on top of the fortnight of iteration-2 genotype work (steps 1-6 and 8) the mechanism facts come from. Compute for Track 2: two laptop runs of about ten minutes against public APIs; no cloud.
16: Question. Given a confirmed compound-heterozygous loss of BUB1B (a stop allele and a hypomorphic kinase-region missense) in a child with mosaic variegated aneuploidy and rhabdomyosarcoma, which market-approved drugs act on the mechanism, and how strong is the evidence for each? Method. Iteration 2 first rebuilt the genotype blind from the raw reads and the eight clinical terms - symptom-only target set with matched decoys, alleles from the reads without the vendor caller, alignment-free genotyping and copy number, a genome-wide likelihood ranking, a knowledge route, and a rank fusion frozen by digest before comparison - and found the same pair first. A structured mechanism card carries the confirmed pair and nine measured facts, the ninth being step 8's mosaic-aneuploidy bound (80 % power at 2-3 % of cells; no autosome above its limit in the sequenced sample). The card drives every query: Reactome expands its seeds to 277 targets; Open Targets, ChEMBL and DGIdb return 359 approved drugs; openFDA, ClinicalTrials.gov and PubMed answer label, trial and literature questions per drug. Every drug on every direction is placed on a five-rung evidence ladder pre-registered before the search, automated tests beside 13 person-curated PubMed rows, inherited class evidence flagged as proxy. Seven claims were registered with refutation conditions before their tests. The pipeline ran unchanged on two decoy cards (same child, gene swapped) as a specificity control. Results. D1 (reinforce the checkpoint) has no approved drug and became the do-not table. D3 (raise BubR1): NAD+ repletion raised BubR1 in BubR1-hypomorphic mice, inherited by niacin and nicotinamide (rung 3); HDAC inhibitors act on BubR1's acetylation switch at class level. D4 (the tumour): lovastatin itself slowed rhabdomyosarcoma cells and a completed paediatric phase-1 trial gave simvastatin in relapsed solid tumours including rhabdomyosarcoma. D2 (aneuploidy stress): chloroquine has a molecule-level cell result, but the direction is argued from the literature only and ranked last, because the sequenced sample shows no aneuploid population for such a drug to act on. Eleven drugs carry a cited mechanism result; fifty more reach the top rung only because they are already in rhabdomyosarcoma trials and are listed, not claimed. The decoy control showed D4's automated stage non-specific (Jaccard 0.25) and D1-D3 specific, and exposed a grading flaw corrected before any verdict; a second pre-registered test showed the measured aneuploid fraction moved no rung. The do-not table names 13 spindle poisons - including standard rhabdomyosarcoma chemotherapy - as a caution for the treating team, because they rely on the very checkpoint that is weakened. Strengths. Pre-registration; a decoy control for a repurposing pipeline; automated and curated evidence never merged; complete lineage; case-agnostic tooling; no patient data in any Track 2 artefact. Limitations. Curated rungs are one reader's; rung 3 is one mouse paper; the aneuploid fraction is measured in a sample whose tissue is unnamed, for whole chromosomes and arms only; the missense's unstable-versus-inactive status is open; DrugBank was not queried; a paediatric pointer is not safety data. These are hypotheses for follow-up, not evidence that any medicine works.
